title: Post-UTME UNILAG
content_provenance: Original practice items authored from the public Post-UTME/use-of-English syllabus. Not a capture of past questions.

items.stem: In the sentence 'The committee reached a consensus after lengthy deliberations', the word 'consensus' means
options: unanimous agreement or harmony of opinion
items.explanation: Consensus refers to a general agreement reached by a group after discussion; it does not imply protest, postponement or disagreement.

items.stem: Choose the option that best completes the sentence: 'Had he studied harder, he ___ the examination.'
items.explanation: The third conditional uses 'had + past participle' in the if-clause and 'would have + past participle' in the main clause to express an unreal past condition.

items.stem: Which of the following is the correct stress pattern for the word 'photograph'?
items.explanation: In British English, 'photograph' is typically stressed on the first syllable (PHO-to-graph), distinguishing it from 'photographer' or 'photographic' which shift stress.

items.stem: Identify the figure of speech in the expression: 'The clouds marched across the angry sky.'
items.explanation: Personification attributes human actions or qualities to non-human objects; 'marched' and 'angry' give the clouds and sky human characteristics.

items.stem: Select the option with the correct order of adjectives: 'She bought a ___ car.'
items.explanation: Standard adjective order in English is size, colour, origin/nationality; so 'big red Italian' follows the conventional sequence correctly.

items.stem: Which of the following sentences is grammatically acceptable in standard English usage?
options: Neither John nor James are coming
None of the girls was present
Each of the boys have a book
The committee have finished its work
items.explanation: With 'none' in formal usage, singular agreement is acceptable; the other options contain clear subject-verb agreement errors.

items.stem: In the context of standard English, 'to beat about the bush' means
items.explanation: The idiom 'to beat about the bush' means to avoid coming directly to the point or to speak indirectly about a matter of concern.

items.stem: Choose the word that is opposite in meaning to 'obscure':
items.explanation: To obscure means to make unclear or difficult to see; its antonym is 'clear', meaning easily understood or visible without ambiguity.

items.stem: Which of the following words contains the /ʃ/ sound (as in 'ship')?
items.explanation: The word 'mission' contains the /ʃ/ sound represented by 'ss'; 'measure', 'vision', and 'pleasure' contain the /ʒ/ sound.

items.stem: Select the option that best fills the gap: 'The manager insisted that the error ___ corrected immediately.'
items.explanation: In a mandative subjunctive construction, the verb remains in its base form regardless of the subject; so 'be corrected' is correct here.

items.stem: In reported speech, which change is correct for 'He said, "I will come tomorrow"'?
options: He said he will come tomorrow
He said he would come the next day
He said he is coming tomorrow
items.explanation: In reported speech, 'will' becomes 'would' and time references adjust; 'tomorrow' becomes 'the next day' in this transformation.

items.stem: Which of the following is a complex sentence?
options: I came, I saw, I conquered.
Although it rained heavily, the match continued.
items.explanation: A complex sentence contains one independent clause and at least one dependent clause; here 'Although it rained heavily' is dependent and 'the match continued' is independent.

items.stem: Choose the word closest in meaning to 'meticulous':
items.explanation: Meticulous means showing great attention to detail and care; 'thorough' best captures this meaning among the given options.

items.stem: Select the appropriate preposition: 'He is proficient ___ Mathematics.'
items.explanation: The correct collocation is 'proficient in' when referring to a subject or skill area; this is standard usage in academic contexts.

items.stem: Which of the following pairs illustrates a homograph with differing pronunciation?
options: lead (metal) and lead (guide) with the same sound
read (past) and read (present) with the same sound
wind (air) and wind (to twist) with different sounds
bow (arrow) and bow (to bend) with the same sound
items.explanation: Homographs like 'wind' (moving air, /wɪnd/) and 'wind' (to twist, /waɪnd/) share spelling but differ in pronunciation and meaning.

items.stem: Identify the type of clause in: 'Whoever comes first will receive a prize.'
items.explanation: In this sentence, 'Whoever comes first' functions as the subject (a noun clause); it does not modify a noun or verb in the typical adjective/adverbial relative sense.

items.stem: Choose the correct form of the verb: 'By next year, she ___ in this school for five years.'
items.explanation: The future perfect continuous tense ('will have been teaching') indicates an action that will continue up to a point in the future.

items.stem: Which of the following sentence pairs is an example of antonymy?
items.explanation: Antonyms are words with opposite meanings; 'hot' and 'cold' clearly represent opposite extremes on the temperature scale.

items.stem: Select the option that best expresses necessity: 'It is necessary for us to leave now.'
items.explanation: The modal 'must' expresses necessity or obligation; it most directly conveys 'it is necessary for us to leave now' among the options.

items.stem: In a formal letter, which of the following is the most appropriate closing?
items.explanation: In formal correspondence, particularly when the recipient's name is unknown, 'Yours faithfully' is the standard and appropriate closing phrase.

items.stem: If x + 5 = 12, then 2x - 3 equals
items.explanation: Solving x+5=12 gives x=7; 2x-3 = 14-3 = 11. Thus the correct value is 11.

items.stem: Solve the following linear equation for x: 3x - 4 = 2x + 5
items.explanation: Subtract 2x: x-4=5; add 4: x=9. The solution to the linear equation is 9.

items.stem: The arithmetic mean of 4, 6, 8, 10, and 12 is
items.explanation: Sum = 4+6+8+10+12=40; count=5; mean = 40/5 = 8. So the average of these numbers is 8.

items.stem: If the area of a rectangle is 48 cm2 and its length is 8 cm, what is its perimeter?
items.explanation: Width = Area/length = 48/8 = 6 cm; Perimeter = 2(length+width) = 2(8+6) = 2(14) = 28 cm.

items.stem: Simplify the expression (x2 - y2)/(x - y) where x is not equal to y
items.explanation: The difference of squares x2-y2 factors as (x+y)(x-y); dividing by (x-y) gives x+y, provided x is not equal to y.

items.stem: Find the value of log base 10 of 1000
items.explanation: Since 10 cubed = 1000, the logarithm base 10 of 1000 equals 3 by definition.

items.stem: In a right-angled triangle, if one leg is 3 and hypotenuse is 5, what is the other leg?
items.explanation: By Pythagoras: other^2 = 5^2 - 3^2 = 25-9 = 16, so other leg is 4.

items.stem: What is the next term in the sequence 2, 6, 12, 20, ...?
items.explanation: Terms follow n(n+1): 1x2=2, 2x3=6, 3x4=12, 4x5=20, so next is 5x6=30.

items.stem: If sin theta = 0.5 and theta is acute, then theta equals
items.explanation: For acute angles, sin 30 degrees = 0.5, which is a standard trigonometric value.

items.stem: Solve the inequality: 2x + 3 < 9
items.explanation: Subtract 3 to get 2x < 6; divide by 2 to get x < 3, which is the solution set.

items.stem: The gradient of the line 2y = 4x + 6 is
items.explanation: Rewrite in slope-intercept form as y = 2x + 3; the gradient (slope) is therefore 2.

items.stem: If a number is increased by 20 percent to become 60, what was the original number?
items.explanation: Let the original number be x; 1.20x = 60, so x = 60/1.20 = 50.

items.stem: Which of the following is a prime number?
items.explanation: A prime number has exactly two positive divisors, 1 and itself. 17 is prime, whereas 1, 9 and 15 are not.

items.stem: Find the value of x if 4^(x+1) = 64
items.explanation: Writing 64 as 4^3 gives 4^(x+1) = 4^3, so x+1 = 3 and therefore x = 2.

items.stem: In logical reasoning, which of the following syllogisms is valid?
options: All A are B; all B are C; therefore all C are A
All A are B; some B are C; therefore all A are C
All A are B; all B are C; therefore all A are C
All A are B; all C are B; therefore all A are C
items.explanation: Transitivity holds: if all A are B and all B are C, then all A are C. The other forms commit common syllogistic fallacies.

items.stem: Which of the following is the capital city of Nigeria?
items.explanation: Abuja became the capital of Nigeria on 12 December 1991, replacing Lagos as the administrative center.

items.stem: The first military coup d'etat in Nigeria took place in
items.explanation: Nigeria's first military coup occurred on 15 January 1966, led by Major Chukwuma Kaduna Nzeogwu.

items.stem: Which of the following rivers is the longest in Nigeria?
items.explanation: The River Niger is the longest river in Nigeria and the principal river of West Africa.

items.stem: The University of Lagos was established in which year?
items.explanation: The University of Lagos was founded in 1962 by an Act of Parliament, making it one of Nigeria's earliest universities.

items.stem: Which of the following countries is NOT a member of ECOWAS?
items.explanation: ECOWAS comprises West African countries; Chad is in Central Africa and is therefore not a member.

items.stem: The current Nigerian national anthem was adopted in
items.explanation: Nigeria's current national anthem, 'Arise, O Compatriots', was adopted in 1978, replacing the earlier anthem.

items.stem: Which body is responsible for conducting elections in Nigeria?
items.explanation: The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) is constitutionally empowered to organize, conduct and supervise elections in Nigeria.

items.stem: The highest court of appeal in Nigeria is the
items.explanation: The Supreme Court of Nigeria is the highest judicial body and the final court of appeal for all decisions.

items.stem: Which of the following minerals is Nigeria the largest producer of in Africa?
items.explanation: Nigeria is Africa's largest oil producer, with petroleum serving as a major foreign exchange earner.

items.stem: The official currency used in Nigeria is the
items.explanation: The Nigerian Naira (NGN) is the official currency of the Federal Republic of Nigeria.

items.stem: Which country shares the longest border with Nigeria?
items.explanation: Nigeria shares its longest land border with Niger Republic, stretching across the northern part of the country.

items.stem: The National Youth Service Corps (NYSC) was established in
items.explanation: NYSC was established by decree No. 24 of 1973 as a means of fostering national unity and integration.

items.stem: Which ethnic group is predominant in Lagos State?
items.explanation: Lagos State is predominantly Yoruba, though it is highly cosmopolitan with people from all ethnic groups.

items.stem: The United Nations agency responsible for education is
items.explanation: UNESCO promotes international cooperation in education, science and culture, and leads global education initiatives.

items.stem: Which colour is NOT part of the Nigerian national flag?
items.explanation: The Nigerian flag consists of two green stripes and one white stripe; red and black are not part of it.

items.stem: For a candidate seeking admission to study Medicine at UNILAG, which of the following UTME subject combinations is most appropriate?
items.explanation: Medicine and related medical courses require Biology, Chemistry, Physics and Use of English as core subjects in the UTME.

items.stem: A student interested in studying Law at UNILAG should have a background in
items.explanation: Law is typically offered to candidates from Arts or Social Sciences backgrounds with subjects such as Literature, Government, CRS or History.

items.stem: Which subject combination is best suited for admission into Electrical Engineering at UNILAG?
items.explanation: Engineering courses require a strong background in Mathematics, Physics, Chemistry and Use of English for the UTME.

items.stem: For Mass Communication at UNILAG, which combination aligns well with the admission requirements?
options: Technical Drawing, Metal Work, Maths, English
items.explanation: Mass Communication in most universities favors Arts subjects such as Literature and Government combined with Use of English.

items.stem: A candidate applying for Computer Science at UNILAG should register for which UTME subjects?
items.explanation: Computer Science requires Mathematics, Physics, Chemistry and Use of English as the standard subject combination.

items.stem: Which combination is most suitable for studying Accounting at UNILAG?
items.explanation: Accounting and related management courses typically require Mathematics, Economics, and another relevant commercial subject plus English.

items.stem: For admission into Pharmacy at UNILAG, the required UTME subjects are generally
items.explanation: Pharmacy, like Medicine, requires Biology, Chemistry, Physics and Use of English in the UTME.

items.stem: Which of the following is the appropriate combination for studying Economics at UNILAG?
items.explanation: Economics programs usually require Mathematics, Economics, and a third social science subject such as Government, plus Use of English.

items.stem: For a candidate aiming for Architecture at UNILAG, which UTME combination is correct?
items.explanation: Architecture requires a science-based combination: Mathematics, Physics, Chemistry and Use of English are typically required.

items.stem: Which subject combination best fits admission into Sociology at UNILAG?
options: Technical Drawing, Wood Work, Maths, English
items.explanation: Sociology falls under the Social Sciences and usually requires subjects like Government, History or Economics, plus Use of English.
